description: 500 questions on Python dictionaries (intermediate to advanced: creation, access, methods, iteration, views, comprehensions, nested structures, counting, sorting, merging, hashing, performance, and coding problems)

questions.answer: No, they are views; convert with list() to get a list

questions.answer: ('b', 2) (removes and returns the last inserted item)

questions.question: What does {'a': 1} | {'a': 99} return?

questions.answer: Yes, merging is left-associative: (a | b) | c

questions.question: What does d = {'a': 1}; d2 = d.copy(); print(d2) produce?

questions.answer: No, it is shallow; nested objects are shared

questions.question: What does d = {'a': [1]}; d2 = d.copy(); d2['a'].append(2); print(d) produce?

questions.question: What does a, b = {'x': 1, 'y': 2}; print(a, b) output?

questions.question: What does list(reversed({'a': 1, 'b': 2})) return?

questions.answer: Yes, reversed() iterates keys in reverse, but dict itself is not a sequence for indexing

questions.question: How many elements can a dict store?
